summary.text: A 54-year-old male presented with recent onset of floaters and flashes in the left eye. He had a history of a laser barrage for a retinal hole in the left eye and, in the fellow eye, laser treatment of a retinal hole with transscleral cryopexy. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/30 in both eyes.

Fundus examination of the left eye showed a large horseshoe tear with an adjacent smaller tear at the temporal periphery over the previous barrage laser, with subretinal fluid, and macular OCT showed a stage 1 epiretinal membrane with a normal foveal contour. Subclinical rhegmatogenous retinal detachment was diagnosed. The patient, not keen on an invasive procedure, was counseled and offered DLP.

He underwent DLP in the left eye and was then regularly followed. After 1 year of regular follow-up he is stable with the laser barrage well containing the detachment, although the subretinal fluid is not yet resolved. No progression in the stage of the epiretinal membrane was detected at subsequent visits.

summary.text: A 60-year-old male came for a regular retina follow-up. He had a history of MIVS in the left eye for a rhegmatogenous retinal detachment along with cataract extraction 1 year back, and a barrage laser in the right eye for a retinal hole 5 years back. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye.

The anterior segment was unremarkable except for an early cataract in the right eye. Right-eye fundus examination showed a normal disc, an attached macula and a temporal subclinical retinal detachment adjacent to the previous barraged hole, anterior to the equator and involving 2 clock hours. The left retina was attached after MIVS.

After discussing his situation and the treatment options with the patient, DLP was done in the right eye for the subclinical detachment and he was kept under close follow-up, with premonitory signs explained. He has completed 1 year of follow-up, is still asymptomatic, the subretinal fluid is persistent, and no progression of the detachment is seen.

summary.text: A 48-year-old female came for a regular ophthalmic examination with no complaints in either eye. She was a known myope using corrective glasses since her teenage. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes, with a refractive correction in each eye, and the anterior segment examination was unremarkable.

The right eye showed an attached retina with a normal disc and macula. In the left eye the disc and macula appeared normal, but a superonasal retinal hole with subclinical retinal detachment was seen spanning over 2 clock hour and anterior to the equator. The detachment was shallow.

The patient was counselled about the left-eye condition, and DLP was done, with some additional laser marks applied surrounding the break. She was followed up regularly, showed no signs of progression, and the detachment is well contained even after more than a year of follow-up.

summary.text: A 20-year-old male presented with diminution of vision in both eyes and blurred vision for a while, especially during outdoor sports activities. He had no history of using corrective glasses. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/30 in both eyes, and the anterior segment examination did not reveal any anomaly.

The right eye showed a normal disc, an attached macula and a retinal hole with subclinical rhegmatogenous retinal detachment in the supertemporal quadrant spanning 2 clock hours and within two-disc diameter posterior to the equator. The left retina was attached. He could not recollect flashes or floaters in the past few days, pointing to an incidental finding.

The prognosis was explained and management options were discussed. DLP was done in the right eye, delimiting the detachment with laser marks applied surrounding the retinal break. The patient has completed over a year of follow-up with no signs of progression seen.

summary.text: A 20-year-old female came for a regular retina checkup. She had a history of using corrective glasses for the past 5 years and had undergone laser barrage for a lattice with hole in the left eye 3 months before her initial presentation. She had no complaints of floaters, flashes, or field defects.

Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes and the anterior segment examination revealed no anomaly. The right eye had an attached macula, a normal disc and multiple peripheral lattices in all quadrants. The left eye had an attached macula and normal disc but a subclinical retinal detachment in the inferotemporal quadrant, with a lasered lattice that appears to be the source.

Barrage laser photocoagulation for the multiple right-eye lattices was advised. For the left eye, DLP was done in a single sitting and the patient was routinely followed up thereafter. She has completed a year of follow-up and the SCRD is stable with no evidence of progression noted.
